question: An engineer must add a new VRF (DC:DC) to the network that runs with Multiprotocol Border Gateway Protocol (MP-BGP) and EVPN. The requirement for the new VRF is to allow communication of network prefixes between PE1 and PE2. Which two sets of steps should be taken to complete the VRF configuration? (Choose two.)
options:
PE1:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:1
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:1
    route-target export 233:2
PE2:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:2
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:1
    route-target export 233:2

PE1:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:1
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:1
    route-target export 233:2
PE2:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:1
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:2
    route-target export 233:2

PE1:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:1
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:1
    route-target export 233:2
PE2:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:1
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:2
    route-target export 233:2

PE1:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:1
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:1
    route-target export 233:1
PE2:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:2
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:1
    route-target export 233:1

PE1:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:1
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:1
    route-target export 233:1
PE2:
vrf context DC:DC
  rd 233:1
  address-family ipv4 unicast
    route-target import 233:2
    route-target export 233:1
theory: In an MP-BGP EVPN/VPN design, each VRF instance carries a Route Distinguisher (RD) purely to make otherwise-identical prefixes unique in the BGP table, while Route Targets (RT) are separate extended communities that control which PE routers actually import a given prefix into their local VRF. For two PEs to exchange the same VRF's prefixes, each PE's route-target export value must match the other PE's route-target import value — they can use the same value symmetrically on both sides, or cross-matching asymmetric values — while the RD itself doesn't need to match between PEs since it only affects route uniqueness, not import/export filtering. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 3 — VXLAN EVPN Route Distinguishers and Route Targets)
